about: Industries and how each one's cost of goods sold (COGS) is made up when a filing prints no cost of sales. The AI names the company's industry from this list and marks which expense lines are COGS by the industry's rule; the program adds them up. Depreciation and amortisation follow FactSet's convention (cost of revenue including D&A, with D&A also shown on its own), so gross profit compares with FactSet's gross income; banks, finance, insurance and REITs keep their own gross expense. Edit in the web app (Settings > Cost of goods sold) or here to change the default for everyone.

industries.name: Manufacturing & industrials
industries.applies_to: Makes and sells products: factories, precision engineering, electronics, chemicals, packaging, building materials, equipment
industries.cogs: Raw materials and consumables used + purchases + changes in inventories of finished goods and work in progress + subcontract and processing costs + production overheads shown as such (factory, freight-in, utilities). Materials always go in. Expenses presented by nature: employee benefits go in too. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out selling and distribution, administrative, research, other operating and finance costs.

industries.name: Trading, distribution & retail
industries.applies_to: Buys goods and sells them on: trading, wholesale distribution, retail stores, e-commerce, commodity trading
industries.cogs: Cost of goods sold: purchases of goods + changes in inventories (inventories consumed or sold) + freight, duties and other costs of bringing goods in. Materials and goods always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out store staff, rental, selling, administrative and finance costs.

industries.name: Food & beverage
industries.applies_to: Restaurants, food courts, catering, bakeries and food and beverage outlets
industries.cogs: Cost of food and beverages: raw materials, ingredients and consumables used + purchases + changes in inventories, and kitchen or outlet staff costs only when the statement puts them in cost of sales. Materials always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out rental, utilities, general staff, administrative and finance costs.

industries.name: Property development & investment
industries.applies_to: Develops and sells properties, or owns and leases them (not a REIT)
industries.cogs: Cost of properties sold (land, construction and development costs recognised) + direct operating expenses of investment properties (property tax, maintenance, property management, utilities) + cost of other operations shown in cost of sales. Construction materials always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out marketing, administrative and finance costs and fair value changes.

industries.name: REITs & business trusts
industries.applies_to: Real estate investment trusts and property or infrastructure business trusts: gross revenue, property expenses, net property income, distributions to unitholders
industries.cogs: Property operating expenses: property tax, maintenance and repairs, utilities, property management fees, leasing and marketing at the properties, and other direct property costs, so that gross profit is the net property income. Leave out the REIT manager's management fees, trustee fees, other trust expenses, finance costs and fair value changes.

industries.name: Construction & engineering services
industries.applies_to: Builds for others: construction, civil and building contractors, engineering, procurement and installation
industries.cogs: Contract costs: materials + subcontractor costs + direct labour + site overheads. Materials always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out administrative, tendering, other operating and finance costs.

industries.name: Shipping, logistics & transport
industries.applies_to: Shipping, offshore and marine services, airlines, logistics, ports, buses, taxis and rail
industries.cogs: Costs of operating the fleet and services: fuel and bunkers, port, airport and handling charges, charter hire and leases of vessels, aircraft or vehicles, maintenance and repairs, crew and other operating staff, inflight, cargo and other direct service costs. Consumables always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out administrative, selling and finance costs.

industries.name: Hotels, leisure & gaming
industries.applies_to: Hotels, serviced residences, resorts, attractions, cinemas, clubs and casinos
industries.cogs: Cost of food, beverages and other goods sold + direct operating costs of rooms, attractions and gaming (direct staff, supplies, gaming taxes and levies) + property operating costs of the hotels and resorts. Supplies always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out administrative, sales and marketing and finance costs.

industries.name: Energy & utilities
industries.applies_to: Power generation, gas, water and waste, oil and gas production and services, renewables
industries.cogs: Fuel, gas and purchased power or water + transmission and distribution costs + operation and maintenance of plants and fields. Fuel and materials always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out administrative and finance costs.

industries.name: Mining, plantations & commodities
industries.applies_to: Mining and quarrying, palm oil and other plantations, agribusiness and commodity processing
industries.cogs: Production costs: mining, harvesting and processing costs + raw materials and commodities purchased + changes in inventories + royalties + plantation upkeep. Materials always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out selling (freight-out), administrative and finance costs.

industries.name: Technology, telecoms & media
industries.applies_to: Telecommunications, software, IT services, data centres, electronics distribution, media and advertising
industries.cogs: Cost of sales and services: equipment and devices sold, interconnect and network costs, content and licence costs, hosting and data-centre costs, direct delivery staff. Equipment and materials always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out research and development, selling, administrative and finance costs.

industries.name: Healthcare & pharmaceuticals
industries.applies_to: Hospitals, clinics, dental and medical services, laboratories, pharmaceuticals and medical devices
industries.cogs: Medical supplies, drugs and consumables used + changes in inventories + doctors' and clinical staff costs and professional fees for services rendered when shown as cost of services. Supplies always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out administrative, marketing and finance costs.

industries.name: Business & consumer services
industries.applies_to: Professional, education, security, cleaning, staffing, facilities management, consultancy and other services
industries.cogs: Cost of services: direct staff costs of delivering the services + subcontractor and outsourcing costs + materials and consumables used in delivering them + other direct project costs. Materials always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out administrative, selling and finance costs.

industries.name: Banks
industries.applies_to: Banks: interest earned and expended, deposits, loans and advances
industries.cogs: Gross expense: financial cost associated with financial income (interest expense) + provision for credit losses (allowances) + insurance service expenses, if any + operating costs. Leave out tax and exceptional items.

industries.name: Finance, leasing & securities
industries.applies_to: Finance companies, leasing, factoring, consumer credit, pawnbroking loans, securities brokers and fund managers
keywords: financial cost associated with financial income
industries.cogs: Gross expense: financial cost associated with financial income (interest on the funds lent out) + provision for credit losses + commission and brokerage paid + insurance service expenses, if any + operating costs. Leave out tax and exceptional items.

industries.name: Insurance
industries.applies_to: Insurers and reinsurers: insurance revenue, insurance service expenses, reinsurance
industries.cogs: Gross expense: insurance service expenses (claims and acquisition costs) + net expense from reinsurance contracts held + insurance finance expenses + operating costs. Leave out tax and exceptional items.

industries.name: Investment holding
industries.applies_to: Holds investments and earns mainly dividends, interest and investment gains; fund vehicles and holding companies
industries.cogs: Only direct costs of the investment income: cost of investments sold when revenue includes their proceeds, and fees paid to manage the investments. Often nothing qualifies: then mark no line and gross profit equals revenue. Leave out administrative and finance costs.

industries.name: Other
industries.applies_to: Anything that fits none of the above
industries.cogs: The direct costs of earning the revenue: materials, goods and consumables, direct labour and subcontractors, and direct operating costs. Materials always go in. Depreciation and amortisation on the face of the statement go in too, as in FactSet's COGS including D&A. Leave out selling, administrative and finance costs.
